one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 1 and 2 hold: their cases are just examples of "limited to the range" and "throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi". Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its regex `'^#+ .*\\b'+n+'\\s*\\('` passes only if each function has a markdown heading in the form `name(`. The words "README.md documents every function" don't require that, so a README that documents the functions in a list or table would fail. That format rule belongs under Advisory. Check 4 also goes too far. "npm test passes" only needs a zero exit, but PASS also requires "the TAP summary shows `# fail 0`". The `node --test` spec reporter doesn't print that line, so a passing run could still fail the check.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. The builder's `npm test` runs, and so do the commands for Checks 1, 2 and 4. Check 3 breaks. It is wrapped in bash double quotes, where `\\` becomes `\`. So JavaScript gets `'^#+ .*\b'+n+'\s*\('`. Inside a JS string literal, `\b` is a backspace character, `\s` becomes `s` and `\(` becomes `(`. The pattern passed to `new RegExp` ends in `s*(`, an unterminated group. That throws a SyntaxError on the first exported name. So Check 3 cannot print PASS for any README, even a correct one. Getting a regex escape through both the shell and a JS string needs `\\\\b`, `\\\\s` and `\\\\(`, or single-quoted shell. As written, this command is broken.

catches-traps.why: I checked all three must_catch items. Item 1 is met: the builder brief adds "### subtract(a, b)" to README.md as well as clamp. Item 3 is met: Check 2 calls clamp with lo greater than hi and fails on "!(e instanceof RangeError)". Item 2 breaks. Check 3 runs inside a bash double-quoted `node -e`, where `\\b`, `\\s` and `\\(` reach JS as '\b' (a backspace character), 's' and '('. The RegExp built from them has an unclosed group, so `new RegExp` throws a SyntaxError on the first exported name. The `exports:` line is never printed, so the check never lists add, subtract, multiply and clamp. It exits non-zero even when every export is documented. It doesn't really check whether subtract has a README entry; it fails every time, so it can never pass.

avoids-must-not.why: Must_not 2 is broken. Check 3 passes only if each exported function has a Markdown heading matching `^#+ .*\bname\s*\(`. Line 3 just asks that README.md "documents every function", so a README covering `subtract` in a bullet or in prose would fail. That makes a specific README layout a requirement, and the demand for "a section with a description" adds more layout. Check 4 also requires the TAP summary `# fail 0`, which may not appear in that form depending on Node's default reporter. Must_not 1 is avoided: Check 3 loops over every export, so it fails when `subtract` is undocumented. Checks 1 and 2 test values and the RangeError type only, not exact messages or parameter counts.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's probes, and the builder brief contains several of them. Step 1 gives input/output pairs "clamp(-5, 0, 100) is 0, clamp(140, 0, 100) is 100, clamp(5, 0, 10) is 5, and lo === hi is allowed". These match Check 1's cases [-5,0,100,0], [140,0,100,100], [5,0,10,5] and [3,3,3,3]. Step 3 names the throw input "clamp(5, 10, 0)", which is Check 2's first case [5,10,0]. Step 2's example "clamp(140, 0, 100) // 100" repeats a Check 1 case again. The builder brief also says the third line "fails today", which echoes Check 3's note about the base. Telling the builder to write tests and run npm test is allowed. But giving it the verifier's own expected-output cases puts the checker's methods in the builder brief, so the criterion is not met.
